# Jubilees Chapter 40 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Joseph's rise; the brothers come to Egypt; the reunion begins

---

**40:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, third week, first year, Pharaoh had two unsettling dreams in one night.

**40:2** Joseph was brought out of prison and brought before Pharaoh. He interpreted both dreams: seven years of extraordinary abundance across Egypt, followed by seven years of devastating famine.

**40:3** Pharaoh made Joseph second-in-command over all Egypt. "There is no one in Egypt above you," Pharaoh told him, "except me."

**40:4** Pharaoh gave him an Egyptian name: Zaphenath-paneah. He also gave him a wife: Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, the priest of Heliopolis.

**40:5** Joseph was thirty years old when he entered Pharaoh's service. He traveled all over Egypt.

**40:6** During the seven good years, Joseph collected grain from every district and stored it in the cities. Then the famine years arrived.

**40:7** Everywhere was hungry — except Egypt. Joseph opened the storehouses and sold grain to Egyptians and to foreigners who came from all over the world.

**40:8** Among those who came were Jacob's sons. The famine had hit Canaan hard too.

**40:9** Joseph recognized them the moment they walked in. They had no idea who he was. He grilled them — harsh questions about their family, about their father, about a younger brother.

**40:10** They told him: yes, our father is alive. Yes, we have a younger brother. Joseph had Simeon tied up and held as collateral: bring the younger brother or don't come back.

**40:11** They went home and told Jacob everything.

**40:12** Jacob was devastated. "First Joseph, now Simeon, and now you want me to risk Benjamin too?" He refused.

**40:13** Reuben tried: "Kill my own two sons if I don't bring him back." Jacob still said no.

**40:14** Finally Judah stepped up: "Send the boy with me. I give you my word — I am personally responsible for him." Jacob agreed and sent Benjamin with his brothers.

**40:15** When they arrived, Joseph saw Benjamin. He excused himself, went to a private room, and broke down crying. He washed his face, composed himself, and came back out.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Jubilees compresses the Genesis 41-43 narrative dramatically. Joseph's emotional breakdown at seeing Benjamin (v.15) is the first crack in his composure and sets up the full revelation in ch.44. The suretyship shift from Reuben (rejected) to Judah (accepted) echoes the Shiloh oracle of ch.38.*
